questions.explanation: Correct: group owners are responsible for confirming that guests in their groups still have a legitimate business need — employee access may be automated by lifecycle workflows, but invited guests are not covered by that automation. The guest's manager, the Global Administrator, and the guest themselves are not the designated reviewer for group guest access.
options: The guest's manager in their home organisation
The Global Administrator, for every group
The group owner, who must confirm the guests still have a legitimate business need for access
Nobody — guest access in groups is never reviewed
questions.question: A group gives guests access to business-sensitive content. Employee access in the tenant is automated with lifecycle workflows. Who is responsible for confirming the guests still need access?
questions.source_quote: Ask group owners to confirm they still need guests in their groups: Employee access might be automated with other identity and access management features such as lifecycle workflows based on data from an HR source, but not invited guests. If a group gives guests access to business sensitive content, then it's the group owner's responsibility to confirm the guests still have a legitimate business need for access.
questions.source_title: What are access reviews? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: access reviews are the tool for the hard cases — when automation is not possible, when a group is used for a new purpose, for business-critical data access, and to maintain a policy exception list with audit proof. They are not a replacement for Conditional Access, not a PIM substitute, and not limited to privileged roles.
options: When automation is not possible, when a group takes on a new purpose, for business-critical data access, and to maintain a policy exception list with regular review
Only when a group has more than 100 members
Only for privileged roles, never for groups or applications
Only when Conditional Access is unavailable
questions.question: Your HR data is not in Entra ID, so dynamic group rules cannot capture who should keep access to a legacy SharePoint site. Which governance capability handles this, and why?
questions.source_quote: When automation is not possible: You can create rules for dynamic membership groups, security groups, or Microsoft 365 Groups, but what if the HR data isn't in Microsoft Entra ID or if users still need access after leaving the group to train their replacements? You can then create a review on that group to ensure those who still need access keeps access.
questions.source_title: What are access reviews? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: lifecycle workflows manage the three phases — Joiner (entering scope), Mover (moving between boundaries, needing more or different access), and Leaver (leaving scope, needing access removed). A fourth 'suspended' phase does not exist in the model, and the phases are not joiner/leaver only.
options: Joiner and Leaver only
Joiner, Mover, and Leaver
Joiner, Mover, Leaver, and Suspended
Onboarding, Offboarding, and Auditing only
questions.question: Your HR team wants one governance capability covering a new hire, an employee changing departments, and an employee retiring. Which lifecycle phases do lifecycle workflows cover?
questions.source_quote: Lifecycle workflows (LCW) are identity governance capabilities that enable organizations to manage Microsoft Entra users across the three phases of a user's lifecycle with an organization: Joiner, Mover, Leaver.
questions.source_title: What are lifecycle workflows? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: workflows consist of tasks and execution conditions — a task is a specific action that runs automatically when triggered, and the execution condition defines the scope of who is affected and when the workflow runs. A workflow is not a single task, not a static group, and not a manual checklist.
options: A workflow is a single task that runs once for one user
A workflow is a static group that never changes
A workflow consists of tasks that run automatically when triggered, plus execution conditions defining who is in scope and when it runs
A workflow is a manual checklist an administrator follows for each hire
questions.question: An architect asks what a lifecycle workflow is made of. Which description is correct?
questions.source_quote: Workflows contain specific processes that run automatically against users as they move through their lifecycle. Workflows consist of tasks and execution conditions. Tasks are specific actions that run automatically when a workflow is triggered. An execution condition defines the scope of who's affected and the trigger of when a workflow will be performed.
questions.source_title: What are lifecycle workflows? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: a mover workflow fits a department change — the user moves between boundaries and may need more or different access. A joiner workflow is for entering scope, a leaver for leaving scope, and on-demand execution is for manual runs, not for an attribute-driven move.
options: A mover workflow, triggered by the move between organisational boundaries
A joiner workflow, because the user is joining a new team
A leaver workflow, because the user is leaving the old team
An on-demand workflow, because department changes cannot trigger workflows
questions.question: An employee moves from Marketing to Sales. They need the Sales groups and apps, and should lose the Marketing-only access. Which lifecycle workflow pattern fits?
questions.source_quote: Mover: When an individual moves between boundaries within an organization. This movement might require more access or authorization. An example is a user who was in marketing and is now a member of the sales organization.
questions.source_title: What are lifecycle workflows? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: you can create, manage, and delete workflows up to a total limit of 100 workflows, and up to 100 custom task extensions. The limit is on workflows, not users, not tasks per workflow, and not executions per day.
options: There is no limit on the number of workflows
You can create up to 100 workflows in total
You can create up to 100 workflows per user
You can create up to 1,000 workflows, but only 100 can be active
questions.question: Your team is designing a large lifecycle automation programme with separate workflows for every department and scenario. What is the workflow limit?
questions.source_quote: With Lifecycle Workflows, you can: Create, manage, and delete workflows up to the total limit of 100 workflows.
questions.source_title: What are lifecycle workflows? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: lifecycle workflows can integrate with Logic Apps tasks to extend workflows for complex scenarios through existing Logic Apps — the extension point for anything the built-in tasks cannot do. It is not a PowerShell-only path, not a replacement of the workflow, and not limited to email tasks.
options: You cannot extend a lifecycle workflow — only the built-in tasks are available
You must replace the workflow with a standalone Logic App and abandon lifecycle workflows
You can integrate Logic Apps tasks to extend the workflow for more complex scenarios through your existing Logic Apps
You can only extend the workflow with email tasks
questions.question: A joiner workflow needs to call an internal HR API that no built-in lifecycle task supports. How do you extend the workflow?
questions.source_quote: Lifecycle workflows can even integrate with the ability of logic apps tasks to extend workflows for more complex scenarios through your existing logic apps.
questions.source_title: What are lifecycle workflows? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: lifecycle workflows can automate assigning and removing access packages for users — the joiner/mover/leaver automation can drive package assignment as part of the lifecycle. It is not limited to email, not limited to leavers, and does not require a separate entitlement product.
options: Yes — lifecycle workflows can be used to automate assigning and removing access packages for users
No — access packages can only be assigned by users requesting them
No — access packages can only be assigned by administrators manually
Yes, but only for leaver workflows, not joiner or mover workflows
questions.question: A joiner workflow should automatically give every new Finance hire the Finance access package on day one, and remove it when they leave Finance. Can a lifecycle workflow do that?
questions.source_quote: Automating Access Package Assignment: Lifecycle workflows can be used to automate assigning, and removing, access packages for users.
questions.source_title: What are lifecycle workflows? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: lifecycle workflows manage static groups, where no dynamic rule is needed, and the workflow rules determine which users are in scope — not which group — so one workflow can manage membership across groups. Dynamic groups need one rule per group and only support attributes they understand; lifecycle workflows also act on the group, not just membership, and can trigger on dates such as days before employeeHireDate.
options: Dynamic group memberships, because they need one rule per group
Lifecycle workflows, because they manage static groups without one rule per group, scope by user attributes including dates, and can act on the group itself
Neither — group membership for new hires must always be manual
Administrative units, because they replace both features
questions.question: HR wants new hires added to their department's static security group three days before their start date, without writing one rule per group. Dynamic group rules cannot express the date trigger. Which approach fits?
questions.source_quote: Lifecycle workflows manage static groups, where you don't need a dynamic group rule. There's no need to have one rule per group. Lifecycle workflow rules determine the scope of users to execute workflows against, not which group. Lifecycle workflows can perform actions on the group, not just the membership.
questions.source_title: What are lifecycle workflows? - Microsoft Entra ID Governance

questions.explanation: Correct: a tenant can have no more than 40 terms. The limit is per tenant, not per user or per policy, and it is not unlimited — a 45-term plan must be consolidated.
options: There is no limit on the number of terms per tenant
The limit is 40 terms per user, with no tenant limit
You can add no more than 40 terms per tenant
The limit is 10 terms per tenant
questions.question: Legal wants 45 separate terms of use documents, one per department policy. What is the tenant limit?
questions.source_quote: You can add no more than 40 terms per tenant.
questions.source_title: Set Up Microsoft Entra Terms of Use with Conditional Access - Microsoft Entra ID

questions.explanation: Correct: users whose consent expires are prompted to reaccept the terms only if their session expired — an expired consent alone does not interrupt an active session. The other options assume an immediate prompt regardless of session state, or that re-acceptance never happens.
options: Users are prompted to reaccept only if their session expired; an expired consent alone does not interrupt an active session
Users are signed out immediately the moment consent expires, even mid-session
Users are never prompted again once they have accepted once, even after expiry
Users are prompted at the next sign-in regardless of whether the session expired
questions.question: A terms of use policy expires consents every 30 days. A user accepted 29 days ago and has an active session on day 31. When are they prompted to reaccept?
questions.source_quote: Users whose consent expires, regardless of the setting used, Expire consents or Duration before re-acceptance required (days) are prompted to reaccept the terms only if their session expired.
questions.source_title: Set Up Microsoft Entra Terms of Use with Conditional Access - Microsoft Entra ID

questions.explanation: Correct: when a new version of the terms is uploaded, the Require reaccept toggle makes users accept the new version next time they sign in — without it, previous consent stays current and only new users or users whose consent expires see the new version. Deleting and recreating is not required, and the new version does not apply instantly to everyone.
options: The new version applies to everyone immediately, with no setting needed
Previous consent is automatically voided for everyone as soon as any new version is uploaded
You must delete and recreate the terms of use policy to force reacceptance
Use the Require reaccept toggle when updating the version, so users are prompted to accept the new version at next sign-in
questions.question: Legal updates the acceptable-use PDF with a new clause and wants every employee to accept the new version. What must the administrator do when uploading it?
questions.source_quote: There's also a toggle option here Require reaccept if you want to require your users to accept this new version the next time they sign in. If you require your users to reaccept, next time they try to access the resource defined in your Conditional Access policy they'll be prompted to accept this new version. If you don't require your users to reaccept, their previous consent stays current and only new users who haven't consented before or whose consent expires see the new version.
questions.source_title: Set Up Microsoft Entra Terms of Use with Conditional Access - Microsoft Entra ID

questions.explanation: Correct: the Intune Enrollment app is not supported for per-device terms of use and must be excluded from any Conditional Access policy requiring terms of use — otherwise enrolment breaks. B2B users are also not supported for per-device terms. The other options invent support that does not exist.
options: The Intune Enrollment app is fully supported for per-device terms of use
Per-device terms of use work for B2B users without restriction
The Intune Enrollment app is not supported for per-device terms of use and must be excluded from the policy
Per-device terms of use require the user to reinstall the Intune app first
questions.question: You enable 'Require users to consent on every device' for terms of use. New device enrolment through Intune starts failing. What is the cause?
questions.source_quote: The Microsoft Intune Enrollment app Application ID: d4ebce55-015a-49b5-a083-c84d1797ae8c isn't supported. Ensure that it's excluded from any Conditional Access policy requiring Terms of Use. Microsoft Entra B2B users aren't supported.
questions.source_title: Set Up Microsoft Entra Terms of Use with Conditional Access - Microsoft Entra ID

questions.explanation: Correct: user acceptance records are deleted when an admin deletes the terms of use, when the tenant loses its P1 or P2 licences, or when the tenant is deleted. They are not deleted on a schedule, not kept forever, and not deleted when a user changes department.
options: Acceptance records are deleted when the terms of use are deleted, when the tenant loses its P1 or P2 licences, or when the tenant is deleted
Acceptance records are never deleted, even if the tenant is deleted
Acceptance records are deleted automatically 30 days after each acceptance
Acceptance records are deleted when a user changes department
questions.question: Your tenant's P1 licences lapse during a renewal gap. What happens to the stored record of who accepted the terms of use?
questions.source_quote: User acceptance records are deleted when: An admin explicitly deletes the terms of use. The tenant loses its Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses. The tenant is deleted.
questions.source_title: Set Up Microsoft Entra Terms of Use with Conditional Access - Microsoft Entra ID

questions.explanation: Correct: the Permission Creep Index is an aggregated metric that periodically evaluates the risk associated with the number of unused or excessive permissions across identities and resources — it measures how much damage identities can cause based on the permissions they have. It is not a count of users, not a compliance score, and not a measure of sign-in frequency.
options: The number of users in the tenant with any admin role
An aggregated metric that periodically evaluates the level of risk associated with unused or excessive permissions across identities and resources
The percentage of sign-ins that use MFA
The number of days since the last access review
questions.question: A governance report cites a rising Permission Creep Index (PCI) for the tenant. What does PCI measure?
questions.source_quote: Permission Creep Index (PCI): An aggregated metric that periodically evaluates the level of risk associated with the number of unused or excessive permissions across your identities and resources. It measures how much damage identities can cause based on the permissions they have.
questions.source_title: What's Microsoft Entra Permissions Management? - Microsoft Entra Permissions Management

questions.explanation: Correct: Permissions Management was designed to be stepped through in order — discover, then remediate, then monitor — because you cannot act on what has not been discovered, and cannot continually evaluate what has not been remediated. The other orders invert the logic.
options: Monitor, remediate, discover
Remediate, discover, monitor
Discover and monitor at the same time, then remediate
Discover, remediate, then monitor — in that order
questions.question: A team adopting Permissions Management wants to start by auto-deleting unused permissions on day one. What order does Microsoft recommend for its three use cases, and why?
questions.source_quote: Permissions Management allows customers to address three key use cases: discover, remediate, and monitor. Permissions Management is designed in such a way that we recommended you 'step-through' each of the below phases in order to gain insights into permissions across your organization. This is because you generally can't take action on what has not been discovered, likewise you can't continually evaluate what has not been remediated.
questions.source_title: What's Microsoft Entra Permissions Management? - Microsoft Entra Permissions Management

questions.explanation: Correct: Permissions Management detected, automatically right-sized, and continuously monitored unused and excessive permissions across Azure, AWS, and GCP — the multicloud CIEM capability. It did not manage on-premises AD, did not issue certificates, and did not replace Conditional Access.
options: It managed on-premises Active Directory group membership
It issued certificates for service principals
It detected, automatically right-sized, and continuously monitored unused and excessive permissions across Azure, AWS, and GCP
It replaced Conditional Access for multicloud sign-ins
questions.question: Before its retirement, what did Microsoft Entra Permissions Management actually do?
questions.source_quote: Permissions Management detects, automatically right-sizes, and continuously monitors unused and excessive permissions.
